statements.statement: Kentucky requires every owner or operator of a motor vehicle registered in Kentucky, or operated in Kentucky with the owner's permission, to keep security for basic reparation benefits (personal injury protection) and for tort liability continuously in force, through an insurance contract or by qualifying as a self-insurer.

The minimum liability security is $25,000 for bodily injury to any one person, $50,000 for bodily injury to all persons in one accident and $25,000 for property damage in one accident, or a single limit of $60,000 per accident.
The required security also includes basic reparation benefits, which pay up to $10,000 for all economic loss from injury to any one person in one accident.

An auto liability policy for a vehicle registered or principally garaged in Kentucky must include uninsured motorist coverage at the KRS 304.39-110 bodily injury limits unless a named insured rejects that coverage in writing.

Kentucky requires an insurer that will not renew a property or casualty policy covered by KRS 304.20-300 to 304.20-350 to mail or deliver written notice to the named insured, with the specific reasons, at least 75 days before the end of the policy period.

Once such a policy has been in effect more than 60 days, the insurer's written notice of cancellation must be mailed or delivered at least 75 days before the cancellation takes effect, or at least 14 days before if the cancellation is for nonpayment of premium.
For a policy period longer than 30 days, the insurer must mail or deliver a notice of the renewal premium, or a bill for it, at least 30 days before the policy period ends.

Once such a policy has been in effect more than 60 days, the insurer's written notice of cancellation must be mailed or delivered at least 75 days before the cancellation takes effect, or at least 14 days before if the cancellation is for nonpayment of premium.
For a policy period longer than 30 days, the insurer must mail or deliver a notice of the renewal premium, or a bill for it, at least 30 days before the policy period ends.

Kentucky requires an insurer that will not renew a property or casualty policy covered by KRS 304.20-300 to 304.20-350 to mail or deliver written notice to the named insured, with the specific reasons, at least 75 days before the end of the policy period.

Once such a policy has been in effect more than 60 days, the insurer's written notice of cancellation must be mailed or delivered at least 75 days before the cancellation takes effect, or at least 14 days before if the cancellation is for nonpayment of premium.

Kentucky requires an insurer that will not renew a property or casualty policy covered by KRS 304.20-300 to 304.20-350 to mail or deliver written notice to the named insured, with the specific reasons, at least 75 days before the end of the policy period.

Once such a policy has been in effect more than 60 days, the insurer's written notice of cancellation must be mailed or delivered at least 75 days before the cancellation takes effect, or at least 14 days before if the cancellation is for nonpayment of premium.

For a motorcycle, Kentucky's required security is fulfilled by the liability coverage alone: $25,000 for bodily injury to any one person, $50,000 for bodily injury to all persons in one accident and $25,000 for property damage, or a single limit of $60,000 per accident. Basic reparation benefits, which are part of the required security for other vehicles, are not required for a motorcycle.

A heating, ventilation and air conditioning contractor in Kentucky must maintain general liability insurance of at least $500,000 and property damage insurance of at least $300,000 from an insurer licensed and approved by the Kentucky Department of Insurance, and no HVAC license is valid without that insurance.

To be licensed as an electrical contractor in Kentucky, an applicant must submit proof of a general liability insurance policy of at least $1,000,000 and proof of compliance with workers' compensation and unemployment insurance laws.

Kentucky requires an insurer that will not renew a property or casualty policy covered by KRS 304.20-300 to 304.20-350 to mail or deliver written notice to the named insured, with the specific reasons, at least 75 days before the end of the policy period.

Once such a policy has been in effect more than 60 days, the insurer's written notice of cancellation must be mailed or delivered at least 75 days before the cancellation takes effect, or at least 14 days before if the cancellation is for nonpayment of premium.
For a policy period longer than 30 days, the insurer must mail or deliver a notice of the renewal premium, or a bill for it, at least 30 days before the policy period ends.

Kentucky requires every owner or operator of a motor vehicle registered in Kentucky, or operated in Kentucky with the owner's permission, to keep security for basic reparation benefits (personal injury protection) and for tort liability continuously in force, through an insurance contract or by qualifying as a self-insurer.

The minimum liability security is $25,000 for bodily injury to any one person, $50,000 for bodily injury to all persons in one accident and $25,000 for property damage in one accident, or a single limit of $60,000 per accident.
Kentucky's workers' compensation law applies to any employer, other than one engaged solely in agriculture, that has one or more employees in Kentucky subject to that law.

Each such employer must insure its liability for compensation with an insurer authorized to write workers' compensation in Kentucky, or prove to the commissioner that it can pay compensation directly and post the security the commissioner requires.

A Kentucky notary public must submit a $1,000 surety bond, issued by a surety or other entity licensed or authorized to do business in Kentucky, and file it with the county clerk within 30 days of receiving the commission.

An individual life insurance policy delivered in Kentucky, other than credit life or a policy under a tax-qualified pension plan, must let the policyowner return it to the company or the agent within at least 10 days after receiving it; the policy is then void from the start and any premium paid is returned promptly.
After the first premium, the policy must allow a grace period of 30 days, or one month of at least 30 days, during which it stays in force while a premium is paid.

hubs.subtitle: Protection for you and your family

intro.text: Personal insurance protects your home, your vehicles, your belongings and your responsibility to other people if you cause an accident or someone is hurt on your property.
Each page below explains one coverage in plain language: what it pays for, what it leaves out, who usually needs it and what affects the price.
Standard home and renters policies exclude flood and earthquake damage, so those are separate policies with their own pages here.
An umbrella policy adds liability limits above your home and auto policies.
As an independent agency, we compare the insurance companies we're appointed with and help you choose coverage that fits your household.

hubs.subtitle: Protection that lets your business grow

intro.text: Business insurance protects your company against claims from customers and the public, damage to your property and vehicles, injuries to your employees and other risks of your work.
Each page below explains one coverage: who needs it, what it protects against, what affects the price and what it does not cover.
Kentucky's workers' compensation law applies to any employer, other than one engaged solely in agriculture, with one or more employees in Kentucky subject to that law.
Some Kentucky trade licenses also require insurance: no HVAC contractor license is valid without the general liability and property damage insurance the law sets.
As an independent agency, we compare the insurance companies we're appointed with to build coverage around how your business operates.
Life insurance pays the people you name when you die, so they can cover a mortgage, debts, everyday bills or final expenses.
Term life covers a set number of years, whole life lasts your lifetime and builds cash value, and final expense is a small whole life policy for funeral and end-of-life costs.
Disability insurance replaces part of your income if illness or injury keeps you from working, and an annuity can turn savings into a stream of income.

In Kentucky, an individual life insurance policy, other than credit life or a policy under a tax-qualified pension plan, must give you at least 10 days after you receive it to return it, and the premium you paid is then returned.
Health insurance helps pay for doctor visits, hospital care, prescriptions and preventive care.
Where your coverage comes from shapes your options: an employer's group plan, an individual or family plan you buy yourself, or a public program.
Each page below explains one option, including group health for small businesses, individual and family plans, dental and vision, and supplemental coverage.

Kentucky's health insurance exchange, kynect, is where Kentuckians can shop for and enroll in individual and family health plans and apply for Medicaid and KCHIP, which people who qualify can join at any time of year.
Tell us what you need and a licensed agent will contact you about your options.
